title: Abu Bakr's will
hook: dying, he names Umar and leaves almost nothing (reported)

segments.voice: Yesterday: riddah, the turning back, and prayer and zakat held together. Your line was holding together.

An old man lies ill, and he asks his daughter a strange question. In how many cloths was the Prophet wrapped for burial? Then another: on what day did the Prophet die? Monday, she says. And what day is it today? Monday again. He hopes, he says, to die before tonight is out. The daughter is Aisha. The father is Abu Bakr, the khalifah, leader of the whole community, and he is arranging his own departure as simply as he can. Today: Abu Bakr.
screen: `HOW MANY CLOTHS?` → `WHAT DAY DID THE PROPHET DIE?` → `ARRANGING HIS OWN DEPARTURE.`

segments.voice: Bukhari keeps the scene. The Prophet, Aisha answers, was wrapped in three white cloths. Abu Bakr looks at the garment he has been wearing in his illness, which has a stain of saffron on it. Wash this one, he says, add two more, and wrap me in them. Aisha protests: but it's worn. And he answers: the living have more right to the new than the dead. It is only for what the body gives back to the earth. The leader of the whole community, asking to be buried in a used garment. The histories add more, and they are clear that these are reports. Tradition says Abu Bakr asked that whatever his household had gained while he held office be handed on to the next leader. When it arrived, the reports describe very little: an animal, a servant, a worn cloth. And they say Umar wept and said, you have made it hard for whoever comes after you. Before he died, the histories also say, Abu Bakr consulted some of the companions and then had it written that Umar would lead after him. Sunni Muslims see this as a rightful choice made by a rightful caliph. Shia Muslims, as earlier days described, see the whole succession differently. The reports themselves describe a man who did not get rich from power. And he was buried in Aisha's room, beside the friend he had followed. So the succession story that began with the day after ends here: a pledge, a speech, a hard season, and a man who left almost nothing. Tomorrow a new part begins, with Umar.
screen: `THREE WHITE CLOTHS.` · `WASH THIS ONE, AND ADD TWO.` · `THE LIVING HAVE MORE RIGHT TO THE NEW.` · `YOU HAVE MADE IT HARD FOR WHOEVER COMES NEXT.` · then, large: `HE LEFT ALMOST NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the things you own that you never use: a drawer, a closet, a shelf. Choose one, a coat, a tool, a book, that someone living needs more than you do, and picture where it could go. The living have more right to the new.
Abu Bakr, who asked to be buried in a worn, washed garment, gave back what his office had gained, and named Umar to lead after him. Today's word.
Your line: he left almost nothing. A worn garment, washed, was enough for him. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims retell Abu Bakr's deathbed request for a washed, worn garment as a lesson in simplicity; his grave lies beside the Prophet's in the mosque at Medina.

chat.says: Abu Bakr led the whole community. What did he ask to be buried in?
options: His worn, washed garment and two more cloths; the living need the new more.
Fine new cloth from the treasury, as fitted the leader of the community.
The Prophet's own cloak, which Aisha had kept safe since his death.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari he asked Aisha to wash his stained garment and add two more: the living have more right to the new than the dead.

khalifah.meaning: a successor; here, Abu Bakr as leader of the community

Aisha.meaning: Abu Bakr's daughter, and the Prophet's wife

Umar.meaning: the companion named to lead after Abu Bakr

notes: Hadith numbers cited from memory; confirm Bukhari 1387 and the burial report (1392 is Umar's request to be buried there; Abu Bakr's burial in the room is in other reports). Fix the citation if needed.

The handing back of gains in office, the items listed, and Umar's words 'you have made it hard for whoever comes after you' are from Ibn Sa'd and other histories; framed as tradition. The items vary by report; confirm.
